title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a complex-analytic curve. E_X is the sheaf of étale (locally biholomorphic) functions f: X → C, i.e. local coordinates. The page continues an enumeration that started on the previous page. For each group G acting transitively on a model space, Grothendieck looks for the sheaf of geometric objects that classifies 'f modulo G', and for the associated two-point cocycle. The cases are PGL(2) on P^1, G_a on E^1, G_m on G_m, then Aff(1) on E^1, then G_m ⋊ Aut(G_m) on G_m. This is the systematic 'pre-Schwarzian / Schwarzian' hierarchy, presumably serving the study of Picard-Fuchs equations and uniformization.

(c) Group Aff(1) = G_m·G_a acting on E^1.
- Define E_X → Conn(ω_X) by f ↦ D_{df}. This is the unique connection on the canonical line bundle ω_X for which the nowhere-vanishing form df is horizontal.
- It factors as E_X → ω*_X (f ↦ df) followed by ω*_X → Conn(ω_X) (ω ↦ the connection making ω flat).
- First step: by (a), E_X / G_a(C) ≅ ω*_X. On a curve every nonvanishing 1-form is locally df with f étale, unique up to an additive constant.
- Second step: by (b), ω*_X / G_m(C) ≅ Conn(ω_X). Every holomorphic connection on a line bundle over a curve is flat. Its local horizontal nonvanishing sections are unique up to a scalar.
- Hence E_X / Aff(1,C) ≅ Conn(ω_X). Affine structures on X correspond to holomorphic connections on K_X, a torsor under ω_X.
- The difference cocycle is D(f,g) = D_{dg} − D_{df} = d log(dg/df) ∈ Γ(ω_X).
- In a local coordinate t: D(f,g) = d(g'/f')/(g'/f') = dg'/g' − df'/f' = (g''/g' − f''/f') dt. This is the difference of pre-Schwarzians, i.e. the affine analogue of the Schwarzian cocycle.

(d) The 'affine group' of G_m, i.e. Aut(G_m)·G_m with Aut(G_m) = Z/2Z.
- It acts on C^× by f ↦ cf (c ∈ C^×) and f ↦ 1/f.
- For f in E^×_X = Et(X, C^×), the form df/f ∈ ω*_X is invariant under scaling and changes sign under inversion.
- Squaring therefore gives E^×_X → (ω_X^{⊗2})*, f ↦ (df/f)^2. This identifies f modulo C^× ⋊ Z/2 with nonvanishing quadratic differentials.
- The page stops here; the implied cocycle would be ((dg/g)/(df/f))^2 ∈ O*_X.
errors: Implicit hypothesis: X is a curve (dim 1). Otherwise E_X/G_a ≅ ω*_X fails, since 1-forms need not be closed, and 'connection on ω_X with df horizontal' must be read differently.
The isomorphisms are of sheaves (local statements), not of global sections.
The (d) part is left incomplete at the bottom of the page; the next page is blank.

ideas.what: Classification of local coordinates modulo Aff(1) by holomorphic connections on the canonical bundle, with cocycle d log(g'/f') = (g''/g' − f''/f')dt
ideas.modern_name: affine structures on Riemann surfaces ↔ connections on K_X; pre-Schwarzian derivative cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Poincaré era); systematized by Gunning (Lectures on Riemann Surfaces 1966; 'On uniformization of complex manifolds: the role of connections' 1978)
ideas.where_published: not known in Grothendieck's published works

ideas.what: Hierarchy of (G, model space) pairs (PGL2/P^1, Aff/E^1, G_a/E^1, G_m/G_m, G_m⋊Z/2/G_m) with corresponding torsors/differential invariants (Schwarzian, connections, 1-forms, quadratic differentials)
ideas.modern_name: (G,X)-structures and their differential invariants; projective differential geometry

ideas.what: C^× ⋊ Z/2 acting on C^× gives nonvanishing quadratic differentials via f ↦ (df/f)^2
ideas.modern_name: half-translation structures ↔ quadratic differentials (multiplicative form via exp)

deep.surprise_reason: Clean but standard exploration of affine/projective-type structures on curves and their cocycles (pre-Schwarzian, quadratic differentials). All of this is classical and well documented (Gunning etc.).
transcription_corrections: Line 'd) Conn E_X "affine" de G_m' should read roughly 'd) Groupe "affine" de G_m : Aut(G_m)·G_m', with Aut(G_m) = Z/2Z written underneath. 'Conn' is a misreading of 'Groupe', and E_X is an inserted correction above it.
'(en fait isomorphisme par a)' is better read as '(en fait isomorphisme par a) [and] E_X ≅ ω*_X via d modulo G_a(C)'; 'et par b)' introduces the second isomorphism.
'connexion canonique[?]' is likely 'connexion de ω_X pour laquelle df est horizontale', with a small insertion above the line.
